name: Ürümqi Tianshan International Airport
before:
The airport for Ürümqi, capital of Xinjiang, 16 km north west of downtown. It handled 29,179,737 passengers in 2025, eighteenth busiest in China, as a hub for China Southern and a focus city for Hainan Airlines.

It is the most capable airport in any of China's five autonomous regions, the only one rated 4F class, which is the category that takes the largest aircraft. Three runways serve the site, two of them 3,600 metres and the third 3,200 metres, and the apron holds over 30 aircraft.

Terminal 1 is worth identifying before travel. After renovation it handles mainly regional Xinjiang routes and low cost carriers including Tianjin Airlines, Capital Aviation and Spring Airlines, with 19 check-in counters and six security channels. It reopened on 1 April 2014 after nearly two and a half years closed.

The airport sits at an elevation of 648 metres and the original terminal dates from 1974.
after:
The airport for Ürümqi, capital of Xinjiang, 16 km north west of downtown. It handled 29.2 million passengers in 2025, the 18th busiest in China.

The airport changed in 2025. It was renamed from Diwopu to Tianshan in March, and passenger flights moved into a new North Terminal, Terminal 4, as the old Terminals 1 to 3 closed. Older guidance that sends clients to Terminal 1 is out of date.

Three runways serve the site, two of them 3,600 metres and the third 3,200 metres. The airport sits at an elevation of 648 metres.

claims.note: Replaces the Terminal 1 paragraph. The Xinjiang government's March 2025 report says the main part of the expansion was about to go into full use, with Terminal 4 and a pair of F-class runways on the north side opening and Terminals 1 to 3 closing or being converted, while the south runway stays for cargo. Wikipedia (current revision, 14 Sep 2026) dates the North Terminal's opening to 17 April 2025 and lists Terminals 1 to 3 as closed. The operator's site (xjairport.com) answered 502 and 405.
